values: Use q19_canola_years_wide.csv. Complete the work in Excel using Power Query and keep the queries attached to the submitted workbook.
Import the file with Power Query and reshape it from wide to long. The result must contain field, year, and yield_bu_ac. State what one row represents.
Change year from text such as yield_2021 to the whole number 2021. Give the query a meaningful name and load the long table to a worksheet.
Create a second query that starts from the long query. Compute mean yield by year, sort from highest to lowest, and report the best year.
Submission check: the workbook should contain the original data, the loaded long table, the yearly summary, and both queries with readable Applied Step names.
Original wide table. Keep this table unchanged. The Excel table is named RawData.
The long table should contain 40 rows: one row for each field–year combination. The yearly summary is derived from the long table.
Answer: 2024 has the highest mean canola yield, approximately 41.96 bu/ac.
This answer is self-contained, so its M code reads the RawData table. On the test, begin with Data → Get Data → From Text/CSV. Use Data → Queries & Connections to inspect live queries.
Select RawData and choose Data → From Table/Range.
The editor shows 8 fields and 6 columns.
Set field to Text and each yield column to Decimal Number.
Identifiers and yields have the correct types.
Select field, then choose Transform → Unpivot Other Columns.
The table has 40 rows and three columns.
Rename Attribute to year and Value to yield_bu_ac.
The output names match the question.
Extract the text after the underscore from year, then set it to Whole Number.
Name the query CanolaYieldsLong and load it as a table.
The long output is visible in Excel.
Create a Reference from CanolaYieldsLong; group by year using Average of yield_bu_ac.
Sort mean_yield descending; name the query MeanYieldByYear and load it.

#"Set column types" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, {{"field", type text}, {"yield_2021", type number}, {"yield_2022", type number}, {"yield_2023", type number}, {"yield_2024", type number}, {"yield_2025", type number}}),
#"Extract numeric year" = Table.TransformColumns(#"Rename columns", {{"year", each Number.FromText(Text.AfterDelimiter(_, "_")), Int64.Type}})
#"Mean yield by year" = Table.Group(Source, {"year"}, {{"mean_yield", each List.Average([yield_bu_ac]), type number}}),
#"Sort best year first" = Table.Sort(#"Mean yield by year", {{"mean_yield", Order.Descending}})
